to cupric, impairs copper uptake in animal models, but this does not necessarily happen in humans.
The ﬁrst stage of copper uptake is its aggregation by the mucus and glycocalyx on the enterocytic microvilli, whence it reaches
membrane-associated reductases (STEAP2 and Dcytb) which convert any residual cupric to cuprous copper for translocation into
the enterocyte. There are at least two mechanisms for enterocytic uptake of copper; one which is dependent on CTR1, which
accounts for 70% or more of uptake, and one which probably uses the divalent metal transporter (DMT1). The former mechanism
involves copper uptake into subapical vesicles in the enterocyte, and because this process occurs in the absence of CTR1, and has not
been associated with DMT1-mediated uptake of other metals, it is thought that copper may be ﬁrst taken up by endocytosis, it is not
